clause_text: Black (c) At least 10% of latest fiscal-year revenue comes from immigration detention, or immigration detainee monitoring or transport, as disclosed in the company's own 10-K: 35% of fiscal-year 2025 revenue (10-K filed 2026-02-20; threshold 10%)
summary: CoreCivic's 10-K for fiscal 2025 states that ICE accounted for 35% ($770.7 million) of its total revenue (29% in 2024, 30% in 2023).
caveat: The 10-K gives ICE's share of total revenue, not a separate "immigration detention" line. This screen treats ICE contract revenue as the clause (c) measure, as in the rule's own example. The 10-K does not split ICE revenue between detention and any other service; the team may want to confirm that reading.

evidence.publisher: CoreCivic, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: For the year ended December 31, 2025, ICE, USMS, and the BOP accounted for 35% ($770.7 million), 18% ($390.6 million), and 1% ($32.2 million), respectively, of our total revenue.
